QUESTION:
I'm going London to Birmingham (about 1 hour 20 minutes) and want to work on the train. Can I book first class at the normal first-class fare?

CANDIDATE A:
Yes. First class may be booked where it is more comfortable for working.

CANDIDATE B:
No. First class is only allowed for journeys over three hours each way, or when it is cheaper than standard.

RESPONSE:
Checked against the policy itself (FIN-07). My earlier notes were wrong on three of these points, so the corrected answers are below.

**1. First class, London to Birmingham (about 1h20): No.**
Section 3 allows first class only if the scheduled journey is **more than three hours each way**, or the **first-class fare is cheaper than the standard fare** when you book. Neither applies here, so book standard class. Wanting to work on the train is not a criterion; my notes were wrong on this. Book through the travel portal at least seven days ahead where possible.

**2. Manchester hotel at £135/night: No, you need approval first.**
Section 6 sets a cap of **£150 only for Greater London**. Elsewhere in the UK, including Manchester, the cap is **£110 per night**, including breakfast and excluding VAT. At £135 you need **written approval from your Practice Head before booking**. My notes wrongly applied the £150 figure everywhere.

**3. The £4 tip: No.**
Section 8 says **discretionary tips and gratuities are not reimbursable**. Only a service charge added automatically to the bill can be claimed. My notes wrongly said tips up to 10% were covered. You can claim the £40 dinner itself, since it falls within the £45 daily overnight meal allowance. You'll need an itemised receipt because it's over £10.

**4. Mileage rate: 45p per mile** for the first 10,000 business miles in the tax year, then 25p per mile. Commuting between home and your normal office doesn't count. My notes had this right.
